children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain why we cannot directly use the SAS area rule to find the area of the triangle.

answer.short: The included angle between the two known sides is not given.
answer.worked: The $64^\circ$ angle is not between the $21\text{ cm}$ and $28\text{ cm}$ sides, so $A=\frac12 ab\sin C$ cannot be used directly.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Using sine rule, find $\angle DEF$ to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{\sin E}{21}&=\frac{\sin64^\circ}{28}\\[8pt]
E&=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{21\sin64^\circ}{28}\right)\\[8pt]
E&\approx42^\circ
\end{align*}$$
The supplementary angle is impossible because it and $64^\circ$ exceed $180^\circ$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Hence calculate the area to the nearest square cm.

answer.worked:
Using the unrounded angle $E$:
$$\begin{align*}
F&=180^\circ-64^\circ-E\\[8pt]
A&=\frac12(21)(28)\sin F\\[8pt]
A&\approx282\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Use cosine rule to find an angle, and hence calculate the area of this triangle to 1 d.p.

spec.description: Dark grey unfilled downward-pointing triangle, horizontal upper edge, three exterior side labels. No vertex labels or angle marks.
spec.mathematics: Upper side 4.3 m; left side 4.7 m; right side 5.6 m.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the angle opposite the $4.3\,\mathrm{m}$ side.
$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{4.7^2+5.6^2-4.3^2}{2(4.7)(5.6)}\\\theta&=\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{34.96}{52.64}\right)\approx48.4^\circ\end{align*}$$
Using the unrounded angle,
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12 ab\sin\theta\\A&=\frac12(4.7)(5.6)\sin\!\left(\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{34.96}{52.64}\right)\right)\\A&\approx9.8\,\mathrm{m}^2\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Calculate the area of these triangles. Answer in square cm to 1 d.p.
(Hint: Use sine rule and angle sum of a triangle)

spec.description: Unlettered source-shaped triangle with left, top-right and bottom-right vertices. 17.7 cm above upper edge, 10.1 cm outside lower-left edge and 74 degrees inside bottom-right corner. No angle arc.
spec.mathematics: 17.7 cm opposite 74 degrees; 10.1 cm opposite top-right angle. Right edge unlabelled. Source is not to scale; coordinate names are not printed.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the top-right angle and $\phi$ the left angle.
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{\sin\theta}{10.1}&=\frac{\sin74^\circ}{17.7}\\[8pt]
\theta&=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{10.1\sin74^\circ}{17.7}\right)\\[8pt]
\phi&=180^\circ-74^\circ-\theta\\[8pt]
A&=\frac12(17.7)(10.1)\sin\phi\\[8pt]
A&\approx85.4\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$
The supplementary value of $\theta$ would make the angle sum exceed $180^\circ$.

spec.description: Unlettered black triangle with top apex and a base rising slightly right; 15.3 cm outside left slope, 48 degrees inside bottom-left corner and 67 degrees inside bottom-right corner. No arcs.
spec.mathematics: Left side 15.3 cm is opposite 67 degrees; bottom-left angle 48 degrees. Remaining sides unlabelled. Preserve source not-to-scale silhouette.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the top angle and $b$ the base length.
$$\begin{align*}
\theta&=180^\circ-48^\circ-67^\circ=65^\circ\\[8pt]
\frac{b}{\sin65^\circ}&=\frac{15.3}{\sin67^\circ}\\[8pt]
b&=\frac{15.3\sin65^\circ}{\sin67^\circ}\\[8pt]
A&=\frac12(15.3)\left(\frac{15.3\sin65^\circ}{\sin67^\circ}\right)\sin48^\circ\\[8pt]
A&\approx85.6\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unlettered tall black triangle with bottom-left, top and right vertices; 75 degrees inside top corner, 18 degrees inside bottom-left corner and 0.53 m outside lower-right edge. No arcs or right-angle marker.
spec.mathematics: 0.53 m opposite 75 degrees; bottom-left angle 18 degrees. Other sides unlabelled. Preserve source not-to-scale silhouette.

answer.worked:
$0.53\text{ m}=53\text{ cm}$. Let $\theta$ be the rightmost angle and $s$ the side opposite it.
$$\begin{align*}
\theta&=180^\circ-75^\circ-18^\circ=87^\circ\\[8pt]
\frac{s}{\sin87^\circ}&=\frac{53}{\sin75^\circ}\\[8pt]
s&=\frac{53\sin87^\circ}{\sin75^\circ}\\[8pt]
A&=\frac12(53)\left(\frac{53\sin87^\circ}{\sin75^\circ}\right)\sin18^\circ\\[8pt]
A&\approx448.7\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$17.3\text{ m}^2$

Use the cosine rule to find the angle at the diagonal, then add the two triangle areas.
answer.worked:
Join the upper-left and rightmost vertices. Let the diagonal be $d\text{ m}$ and the angle between the $4\text{ m}$ and $2.5\text{ m}$ sides be $\theta$.
$$\begin{align*}
d^2&=5^2+6^2-2(5)(6)\cos65^\circ\\[8pt]
\theta&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{4^2+2.5^2-d^2}{2(4)(2.5)}\right)\\[8pt]
A&=\frac12(5)(6)\sin65^\circ+\frac12(4)(2.5)\sin\theta\\[8pt]
A&\approx17.3\text{ m}^2
\end{align*}$$

content.prompt:
Yorker ($Y$) is 134 km due east of Vendor ($V$).
Xena ($X$) is on a bearing of $232^\circ$ from Yorker and is also 85 km from Vendor.
$\angle VXY$ is an obtuse angle. Find the bearing of Xena from Vendor.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
\angle VYX &= 270^\circ-232^\circ=38^\circ \\
\frac{\sin\angle VXY}{134} &= \frac{\sin38^\circ}{85} \\
\sin\angle VXY &= \frac{134\sin38^\circ}{85}
\end{align*}$$
$\angle VXY$ is obtuse.
$$\begin{align*}
\angle VXY &= 180^\circ-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{134\sin38^\circ}{85}\right) \\
\angle YVX &= 180^\circ-38^\circ-\angle VXY \\
\text{Bearing} &= 90^\circ+\angle YVX \\
&\approx 128^\circ
\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Black perspective cube with front face ADHE and rear face BCGF displaced upwards and rightwards. BF, FG and EF are dashed; all other cube edges and triangle RST are solid. R, S and T are dark midpoint dots on AB, FG and EH. Preserve all eleven italic point labels, with S below-left and F above-right. No angle arc, auxiliary Q, midpoint ticks or solution labels.
spec.mathematics: Cube side length 10. R=(A+B)/2, S=(F+G)/2, T=(E+H)/2 in the affine projection. Numerical 10 labels occur above BC, left of AE and below-right of HG. Requested angle TRS has vertex R.

answer.short:
$48.2^\circ$

Use Pythagoras to find the sides of the triangle inside the cube, then apply the cosine rule.
answer.worked:
Let $Q$ be the midpoint of $EF$. In right triangle $RQT$:
$$\color{#268cff}\begin{align*}ST&=10\\[8pt]RQ&=10,\qquad QE=ET=5\\[8pt]QT&=\sqrt{5^2+5^2}=\sqrt{50}\\[8pt]RT&=\sqrt{10^2+(\sqrt{50})^2}=\sqrt{150}\end{align*}$$
By symmetry, $RS=\sqrt{150}$.
Using the cosine rule in $\triangle RST$:
$$\color{#268cff}\begin{align*}\cos\angle TRS&=\frac{(\sqrt{150})^2+(\sqrt{150})^2-10^2}{2\times\sqrt{150}\times\sqrt{150}}\\[8pt]\cos\angle TRS&=\frac{2}{3}\\[8pt]\angle TRS&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\\[8pt]\angle TRS&=48.189685\ldots^\circ\\[8pt]\angle TRS&\approx48.2^\circ\end{align*}$$

Which equation should be used to obtain the value of $x$ in this triangle?

content.prompt:
The diagram shows an isosceles triangle with an area of $42\text{ cm}^2$ and equal sides of length $x\text{ cm}$.
The angle between the equal sides is $42^\circ$.

Which of the following expressions represents the length of the equal sides?

(A) $\frac{x}{\sin(69^\circ)} = \frac{42}{\sin(42^\circ)}$
(B) $42^2 = x^2 + x^2 - 2x^2 \times \cos(42^\circ)$
(C) $\frac{x^2 \times \cos(48^\circ)}{2} = 42$
(D) $x = \frac{84}{\sin\left(\frac{42\pi}{180}\right)}$

answer.short:
C

Substitute into $A=\frac12ab\sin C$, then use $\sin(42^\circ)=\cos(48^\circ)$.
answer.worked:
Using the area formula for a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12ab\sin C\\42&=\frac12x^2\sin(42^\circ)\end{align*}$$
Since $\sin(42^\circ)=\cos(48^\circ)$:
$$\begin{align*}42&=\frac{x^2\cos(48^\circ)}{2}\end{align*}$$
The answer is C.

content.prompt:
On a golf course, the tee is a distance of $130$ metres due west from the hole.
On her first shot, Kelly hits the ball $100$ metres but not at the correct angle.
On her second shot she hits the ball $35$ metres and gets it in the hole.
On what bearing, $\alpha$, did she hit her first shot?
Give your answer correct to the nearest degree.

answer.short:
$081^\circ$

Use the cosine rule to find the angle between the first shot and the tee–hole line, then subtract it from $90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the angle between Kelly's first shot and the easterly direction from the tee to the hole.
$$\begin{align*}
\cos\theta &= \frac{100^2+130^2-35^2}{2\cdot100\cdot130} \\
\theta &\approx 9.07^\circ
\end{align*}$$
Since bearings are measured clockwise from north:
$$\begin{align*}
\alpha &= 90^\circ-\theta \\
&\approx 90^\circ-9.07^\circ \\
&\approx 80.93^\circ
\end{align*}$$
Therefore the bearing is $081^\circ$.

An aircraft took off from an airport on an angle of elevation of $30^\circ$ until it reached a maximum height of $12\,000$ metres.
The aircraft then descended on an angle of depression of $20^\circ$ to a new height of $9000$ metres.

answer.worked:
Let $a$ be the distance from the airport to the point of maximum height, and $b$ the distance from there to the new height. The vertical drop is $12\,000-9000=3000$ m.
$$\begin{align*}a&=\frac{12\,000}{\sin 30^\circ}=24\,000\text{ m}\\b&=\frac{3000}{\sin 20^\circ}\approx 8771.41\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
The angle between the two flight paths at the maximum height is $180^\circ-30^\circ-20^\circ=130^\circ$. Let $x$ be the distance from the airport to the aircraft. By the cosine rule:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=24\,000^2+8771.41^2-2(24\,000)(8771.41)\cos 130^\circ\\x&\approx 30\,390\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
The distance is $30\,390$ m.

answer.short:
$3.2\text{ cm}^2$

Split the logo into triangles $ABD$ and $BCD$ along $BD$; use the cosine rule for $BD$ and $\angle BCD$, then $A=\frac12ab\sin C$.
answer.worked:
Construct diagonal $BD$.
$$\begin{align*}
BD^2 &= 3^2+2^2-2(3)(2)\cos 60^\circ \\
&= 9+4-12\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\
&= 7 \\
BD &= \sqrt{7}
\end{align*}$$
The area of $\triangle ABD$ is:
$$\begin{align*}
A_{ABD} &= \frac{1}{2}(3)(2)\sin 60^\circ \\
&= \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2} \\
&\approx 2.598
\end{align*}$$
Let $C=\angle BCD$.
$$\begin{align*}
\cos C &= \frac{1.4^2+4^2-(\sqrt{7})^2}{2(1.4)(4)} \\
&= \frac{10.96}{11.2} \\
C &\approx 11.88^\circ
\end{align*}$$
The area of $\triangle BCD$ is:
$$\begin{align*}
A_{BCD} &= \frac{1}{2}(4)(1.4)\sin 11.88^\circ \\
&\approx 0.576
\end{align*}$$
Therefore:
$$\begin{align*}
A &= A_{ABD}+A_{BCD} \\
&\approx 2.598+0.576 \\
&\approx 3.174 \\
&\approx 3.2
\end{align*}$$
The area of the logo is $3.2\text{ cm}^2$.

content.prompt:
The diagram shows a park consisting of two equilateral triangles.
The shaded triangle is a grassed section.
All measurements on the diagram are in metres.
How long will it take to mow the grassed section if it takes $5$ minutes to mow $20 \text{ m}^{2}$?
Give your answer to the nearest minute.

answer.short:
$7$ minutes

Find the shaded side with the cosine rule in a corner triangle, then use $A=\frac12 c^2\sin 60^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The large triangle has side $9+3=12 \text{ m}$, so each angle is $60^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}c^2 &= 9^2 + 3^2 - 2(9)(3)\cos 60^{\circ} \\ &= 81 + 9 - 27 \\ &= 63 \\ \text{Area} &= \frac{1}{2}(63)\sin 60^{\circ} \\ &\approx 27.2798 \text{ m}^{2} \\ \text{Time} &= \frac{5}{20}\times 27.2798 \\ &\approx 6.82 \text{ minutes} \\ &\approx 7 \text{ minutes} \end{align*}$$

A tower is built on flat ground.

$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{Area}(\triangle ABC)&=\operatorname{Area}(\triangle AED)=\frac12(5)(5)\sin108°\\[8pt]AC^2=AD^2&=5^2+5^2-2(5)(5)\cos108°\\\angle CAD&=108°-36°-36°=36°\\[8pt]\operatorname{Area}(\triangle ADC)&=\frac12(50-50\cos108°)\sin36°\\[8pt]\operatorname{Area}(ABCDE)&=25\sin108°+\frac12(50-50\cos108°)\sin36°\\[8pt]\operatorname{Area}(ABCDE)&\approx43.0\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
